question: Elena Novak is a multiple World Championship medallist. Before the 200m freestyle final at a major international meet, she said: "I've trained harder than anyone else here - this is my moment, I know I can do this." Analyse Elena Novak's statement using Bandura's model of self-efficacy and Vealey's model of self-confidence.
markScheme:
AO1 - Knowledge of Bandura's model of self-efficacy and Vealey's model of self-confidence. Bandura called situation-specific self-confidence self-efficacy, which can predict actual performance when the necessary skills and incentives are present. Self-efficacy is influenced by four factors: performance accomplishments (most dependable source, based on previous success), vicarious experiences (watching similar others succeed), verbal persuasion (encouragement from others), and emotional arousal (how a performer interprets their own arousal). Vealey's model looks at trait confidence, state confidence, and competitive orientation (how much a performer is drawn to challenging situations); these combine to influence confidence in the objective sport situation.
AO2 - Application. Bandura's performance accomplishments factor explains Elena's high self-efficacy, as she is a highly successful, multiple-medal-winning swimmer. Vealey's state confidence relates to Elena's belief that her ability will bring success in this specific race, directly determining the quality of her performance. Trait confidence is a stable personality trait which is harder to establish from the statement alone.
AO3 - Analysis/evaluation. Performance accomplishments in relation to Bandura's model are evident from her statement 'I've trained harder than anyone else', reflecting past preparation. Vealey's competitive orientation is reflected in her statement 'this is my moment', suggesting she is drawn to the challenge. It is difficult to fully analyse trait confidence and competitive orientation without further knowledge of Elena's personality, which can only be implied from a single statement.
Credit other relevant analysis.
Max 15 marks.

question: Elite performers may display different levels of confidence. Explain how learned helplessness can affect the performance of an individual.
markScheme:
3 marks for 3 of:
A. Performer perceives failure is inevitable / only option
B. Feels they have no control over the situation
C. Causes avoidance behaviour / no task persistence / giving up / lack of effort
D. Causes global / general learned helplessness - general sporting situations, eg 'not good at racket sports'
E. Causes specific/situational learned helplessness - specific sporting situations, eg 'not good at serving to win the match'
Max 3 marks.

question: Suggest strategies a coach could use to avoid a performer experiencing learned helplessness.
markScheme:
4 marks for 4 of:
A. Performance accomplishments / success from previous performances / reminding performer of previous success
B. Ensure success / gradually increase task difficulty / make task easier / avoid failure
C. Vicarious experiences / watching successful performances
D. Verbal persuasion / encouragement / positive feedback / reinforcement from coach
E. Control emotional arousal / stress management techniques / mental rehearsal / establish set routines
F. Set goals / targets / performance goals rather than outcome goals / reduce importance of the outcome
G. Avoid social comparison with other performers
H. Use attributions correctly / attribution retraining / encourage self-serving bias
Max 4 marks.

question: The coach of an elite volleyball team has noticed a recent decline in the number of successful serves during matches. This has led to a reduction in the players' confidence. Evaluate how effective the use of variable practice and Bandura's model of self-efficacy would be when improving the serving success and confidence of the team.
markScheme:
AO1 - Knowledge of variable practice and Bandura's model of self-efficacy. Variable practice involves varying how a skill is practised in different situations, useful when the skill is open and the environment unpredictable. Self-efficacy is influenced by four factors: performance accomplishments, vicarious experience, verbal persuasion, and emotional arousal.
AO2 - Application to the volleyball coach. Variable practice would involve varied serving drills - floating serves, jump serves, targeting different zones of the court, and introducing opposition to replicate match pressure. Self-efficacy application: coach could show players footage of successful serves (performance accomplishments), give accurate demonstrations (vicarious experience), praise successful serves in practice (verbal persuasion), and use visualisation before serving to control anxiety (emotional arousal).
AO3 - Evaluation of effectiveness. Variable practice can mimic match situations where serving has been poor, adding variety that may increase motivation; starting practices at a lower level of demand and increasing difficulty can build confidence that transfers to harder situations, especially with positive feedback. However, as elite performers, massed practice could also be beneficial since the team are fit and motivated and could interpret kinaesthetic feedback without extrinsic input; massed practice may suit the closed skill of serving better than variable practice. Variable practice is time consuming and could place unnecessary demands on players, potentially worsening confidence issues.
Credit other relevant evaluative points.
Max 15 marks.

question: During a golf coaching session, a coach hears one of the performers saying: "I just can't hit the fairway anymore." Suggest how the golfer is likely to respond to the rest of the session. Refer to learned helplessness in your answer.
markScheme:
AO1 (sub-max 1 mark):
- Performer appears to have situation specific learned helplessness.
AO2 (sub-max 2 marks):
- Performer appears to perceive that failure is inevitable / only option / will always miss the fairway.
- Performer believes they have no control over their ability to drive the ball straight.
- May cause 'avoidance behaviour' / refuse to hit drives / reduced task persistence / giving up / lack of effort.
- Potentially caused by attributing failure to ability / internal stable factors, eg 'I can't drive because of my ability'.
Accept any other suggestion. Answers must refer to learned helplessness.
Max 3 marks.

question: A gymnast is suffering a drop in self-efficacy, having lost situation specific confidence in their ability to perform a beam dismount effectively. Evaluate how appropriate it would be for a coach to concentrate on past performance accomplishments by designing tasks to ensure the gymnast can successfully complete the dismount.
markScheme:
AO1 (sub-max 1 mark):
- Past performance accomplishments are one of the four factors which affect self-efficacy.
AO2 (sub-max 2 marks):
- No definitive proof that this factor is more appropriate than the others (emotional arousal / verbal persuasion / vicarious experiences).
- May need to be used in conjunction with the other factors to be effective.
- Past performance accomplishments may need to be used alongside appropriate goals / attribution retraining / stress management techniques / avoidance of social comparison to be successful.
- Practice designed to ensure success may be artificial and counterproductive, eg use of a spotting harness / false sense of success.
Accept any other relevant evaluative point. Answers must relate to tasks designed to ensure the gymnast successfully completes the dismount.
Max 3 marks.

question: Using an example from archery, explain Vealey's model of sports confidence.
markScheme:
Award one mark for each of the following points (max 5 marks):
- Objective sport situation is a specific skill (not the whole activity), eg shooting a single arrow in a ranking round
- Trait sport confidence (SC-Trait) is the archer's innate/stable level of confidence
- SC-Trait affects state sport confidence (SC-State)/self-efficacy, eg the archer's confidence in that specific shot depends on their underlying trait confidence
- Competitive orientation - the level of competitiveness the archer has/the challenging goals they set themselves
- State sport confidence (SC-State) is confidence in that specific situation/environment and is changeable, eg the archer's confidence for that particular arrow
- Behavioural response - the action/performance outcome, eg the archer releases the arrow and it lands in the inner ring
- Subjective outcome - how the archer judges/interprets the outcome, eg they judge that it was a good, controlled shot
- Subjective outcomes affect future SC-Trait/future competitive orientation, eg positive subjectivity leads to mastery orientation, negative subjectivity can lead to learned helplessness
Max 5 marks.

question: How does 'Objective Sporting Situation' affect confidence according to Vealey's model of sports confidence, using an example from squash?
markScheme:
Award one mark for each of the following points (max 4 marks):
- Combines the skill being performed with the situation it is performed in, eg serving to start a rally in a squash match
- A previously successful skill increases confidence
- A familiar situation, eg playing on a home court, increases confidence
- Allows the performer to evaluate the outcome of the shot
- Can increase confidence for the next point/match
- Maintains effort and task persistence
Max 4 marks.

question: All cross country running teams will experience victories and defeats. Outline strategies that can be used to avoid learned helplessness.
markScheme:

B - General/global learned helplessness - failure is inevitable in all events or equivalent
C - Specific learned helplessness - failure is inevitable in certain situations or equivalent
(B and C must be explained to be awarded marks)
D - Develop self-efficacy/self-confidence/self-esteem
E - Attribution retraining
F - Avoid social comparisons
G - Goal setting/set performance/process/task orientated goals rather than outcome goals
H - Mental rehearsal/visualisation/imagery
I - Provide opportunities for success
J - Positive feedback/reinforcement/peer support
K - One-to-one attention
L - Observe demonstrations by others of similar ability/vicarious experiences
M - Positive self-talk/thought stopping
Max 8 marks.

question: Leaders and coaches have an important role in developing the performance of their skaters. Explain the term self-efficacy and outline the impact of positive vicarious experiences on a figure skater.
markScheme:

G - Verbal persuasion (must be named for explanation points D, F, H and J to be credited)

I - Emotional arousal (must be named for explanation points D, F, H and J to be credited)

question: Marcus Delaney recently won the national time-trial title and a stage of a multi-day amateur tour in the same season. Suggest strategies that can be used to develop high levels of self-efficacy.
markScheme:
